questions.question: Narcondam Island is located in:

__
 
• **Narcondam Island** is a small volcanic island located in the **Andaman Sea**, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India.
 
• The island is situated to the northeast of the main Andaman Islands and is a part of the Andaman district.
 
• Narcondam Island is an extinct volcanic island and is the second volcanic island in India after Barren Island.
 
• The island is known for its unique biodiversity and is home to the **Narcondam Hornbill**, a bird species endemic to the island.
 
• The Andaman Sea, where Narcondam Island is located, lies to the east of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and is part of the northeastern Indian Ocean.

• The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean bounded by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the west, Myanmar to the north, Thailand to the east, and the Malay Peninsula to the southeast.
 
• It is known for its rich biodiversity and is part of the Indo-Pacific region, which supports a variety of marine life.
 
• It is an important route for international maritime trade connecting the Indian Ocean with the Pacific via the Strait of Malacca.

• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a group of islands located at the southeastern edge of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• They are a Union Territory of India and consist of 572 islands, of which 37 are inhabited.
 
• The islands are known for their strategic importance, rich biodiversity, and indigenous tribes such as the Jarawas and Sentineleses.

questions.question: In a bag containing red, green, and pink tokens, the ratio of red to green tokens is 7 : 4, while the ratio of pink to red tokens is 20 : 11. What is the ratio of green to pink tokens?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Identify the **common token** which is **Red**.

Ratio 1 (Red : Green) = 7 : 4 | Ratio 2 (Pink : Red) = 20 : 11.

Multiply Ratio 1 by 11 and Ratio 2 by 7 to make **Red** equal (77).

New Red : Green = 77 : 44 and Pink : Red = 140 : 77.

Green : Pink = 44 : 140 = 11 : 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 35.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Red (R)** to **Green (G)** = 7 : 4

Ratio of **Pink (P)** to **Red (R)** = 20 : 11

**Formula Used:**

To find the combined ratio, equalize the value of the common term (Red).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec7986be39198b894467402c950be9dac6dd83e6cd84619a7a7c4ea7391c0fc3.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ R / G = 7 / 4 ⇒ G / R = 4 / 7

⇒ P / R = 20 / 11

⇒ To find G : P, we can use (G / R) × (R / P)

⇒ G / P = (4 / 7) × (11 / 20)

⇒ G / P = (4 × 11) / (7 × 20)

⇒ G / P = 44 / 140

⇒ Divide both by 4: G / P = 11 / 35

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 35.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a:b and c:d is found by multiplying the corresponding terms: (a×c) : (b×d).

Equalizing Ratios

If a:b and b:c are given, multiply the first ratio by the 'b' value of the second, and the second ratio by the 'b' value of the first to get a:b:c.

Reciprocal Ratio

The reciprocal ratio of a:b is b:a. This is useful when the required output order is different from the given data.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the distribution of elements in the periodic table?

options.text: There is a zig-zag line separating metals and non-metals.
Metals are located on the left side.
Metalloids are scattered randomly throughout the table.
Non-metals are on the top right corner.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metalloids are scattered randomly throughout the table**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Metalloids are not scattered randomly in the periodic table; they are positioned along a **zig-zag line known as the "stair-step line."**
 
• This zig-zag line separates metals on the left side and non-metals on the right side of the periodic table.
 
• Metalloids exhibit properties intermediate between metals and non-metals, and they include elements like boron, silicon, arsenic, and tellurium.
 
• The periodic table is structured systematically, grouping elements based on their chemical properties, atomic number, and electron configuration.
 
• Non-metals are predominantly located in the top right corner of the periodic table, while metals occupy the left side and center.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Table Structure:**

 
 
• The periodic table is divided into groups (columns) and periods (rows) based on atomic number and electron configuration.
 
• Groups indicate elements with similar chemical properties, while periods represent elements with increasing atomic numbers.
 
 
 
• **Metals:**
 
 
• Metals are found on the left and center of the periodic table and are characterized by properties like malleability, ductility, and good conductivity of heat and electricity.
 
• Examples include iron, copper, and aluminum.
 
 
 
• **Non-Metals:**
 
 
• Non-metals are located on the top right corner of the periodic table and exhibit properties like poor conductivity and brittleness.
 
• Examples include oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur.
 
 
 
• **Metalloids:**
 
 
• Metalloids are elements that have properties of both metals and non-metals, positioned along the zig-zag line.
 
• Examples include boron, silicon, and arsenic.
 
 
 
• **Zig-Zag Line:**
 
 
• The zig-zag line or stair-step line separates metals from non-metals and highlights the position of metalloids in the periodic table.
 
• It serves as a visual guide to understanding the classification of elements.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 7 km/hr and the speed of the stream is 5 km/hr. A man rows to a place at a distance of 52.8 km and comes back to the starting point. Find the total time (in hours) taken by him.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Downstream Speed** = 7 + 5 = 12 km/hr

**Upstream Speed** = 7 − 5 = 2 km/hr

**Total Time** = (Distance ÷ Downstream Speed) + (Distance ÷ Upstream Speed)

**Total Time** = (52.8 ÷ 12) + (52.8 ÷ 2) = 4.4 + 26.4 = 30.8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 30.8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5883fe75e5b324991a239bfca78cd7a9bd29090f40e48dd85a4da6fde466e919.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 7 km/hr

Speed of stream (v) = 5 km/hr

One-way distance (D) = 52.8 km

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (Sd) = u + v

Upstream Speed (Sᵤ) = u − v

Total Time = Tdₒwₙ + Tᵤₚ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sd = 7 + 5 = 12 km/hr

⇒ Sᵤ = 7 − 5 = 2 km/hr

⇒ Time taken downstream = 52.8 ÷ 12 = 4.4 hours

⇒ Time taken upstream = 52.8 ÷ 2 = 26.4 hours

⇒ Total time = 4.4 + 26.4 = 30.8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 30.8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed of Boat

The average speed for a round trip is calculated as (Sd × Sᵤ) / u, where u is speed in still water.

Finding u and v from speeds

Speed in still water (u) = (Sd + Sᵤ) ÷ 2 and Speed of stream (v) = (Sd − Sᵤ) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

In downstream, the stream helps the boat (addition), while in upstream, the stream opposes the boat (subtraction).</p

questions.question: The greatest number that divides 152 and 181 leaving remainders 2 and 6, respectively, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the **remainders** from the **given numbers**: 152 − 2 = 150 and 181 − 6 = 175.

Find the **HCF** of 150 and 175.

150 = 25 × 6 and 175 = 25 × 7.

The highest common factor is 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d238d96bde446d1ad62e8bf753c1271f54ee8b7ca1028eec5495044344945478.png] 

**Given:** Numbers are 152 and 181; Remainders are 2 and 6 respectively.

**Formula:** Greatest number dividing x, y leaving remainders a, b = HCF(x − a, y − b).

⇒ First number = 152 − 2 = 150

⇒ Second number = 181 − 6 = 175

⇒ Prime factors of 150 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 2 × 3 × 5²

⇒ Prime factors of 175 = 5 × 5 × 7 = 5² × 7

⇒ HCF(150, 175) = 5² = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF with remainders

To find the **greatest number** that divides several numbers leaving different remainders, subtract the remainders from the respective numbers and calculate their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

LCM with same remainder

The **least number** which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder 'r' in each case is **LCM(x, y, z) + r**.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of (a/b, c/d) = **HCF(a, c) ÷ LCM(b, d)**.</p

questions.question: The tripartite struggle for Kannauj was among the:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tripartite struggle for Kannauj was a power struggle between three major dynasties: **Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Kannauj, located in present-day Uttar Pradesh, was a strategically significant city due to its location on the Ganga trade route and its historical importance.
 
• The struggle began in the 8th century and continued into the 9th century, as each dynasty sought to control Kannauj to assert dominance over Northern India.
 
• The Gurjara-Pratiharas, under rulers such as Nagabhata I and Mihira Bhoja, played a key role in the struggle by frequently contesting the Palas and Rashtrakutas.
 
• The Rashtrakutas, led by rulers like Dhruva Dharavarsha and Govinda III, launched northern expeditions to claim Kannauj, intensifying the conflict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pala Dynasty:**

 
 
• Founded by Gopala in the 8th century, the Pala Empire was known for its patronage of Buddhism and significant contributions to art and education.
 
• The Palas ruled over Bengal and Bihar, with Dharampala and Devapala being prominent rulers during the tripartite struggle.
 
 
 
• **Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty:**
 
 
• This dynasty emerged in western and northern India, with its capital shifting to Kannauj during its peak.
 
• Known for its resistance to Arab invasions, the Pratiharas played a significant role in preserving Indian culture during this era.
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:**

• Their rulers often launched northern campaigns, bringing them into conflict with the Palas and Pratiharas.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Kannauj:**
 
 
• Kannauj was a key center of trade, administration, and cultural exchange in medieval India.
 
• Control over Kannauj symbolized political supremacy over Northern India, making it a coveted prize for the rival dynasties.

questions.question: The roots of the quadratic equation 7x²− 10x + 3 = 0 are:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, if the sum of **coefficients** (a + b + c) equals 0, then the **roots** are always **1** and **c/a**.

In the equation 7x² − 10x + 3 = 0, coefficients are a = 7, b = −10, and c = 3.

Sum: 7 + (−10) + 3 = 0.

Therefore, the roots are 1 and 3/7.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 and 3/7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quadratic Equation: 7x² − 10x + 3 = 0

**Method: Factorization by splitting the middle term**

To factorize, we need two numbers that multiply to (7 × 3 = 21) and add up to −10. These numbers are −7 and −3.

⇒ 7x² − 7x − 3x + 3 = 0

⇒ 7x(x − 1) − 3(x − 1) = 0

⇒ (x − 1)(7x − 3) = 0

Now, set each factor to zero:

⇒ x − 1 = 0 → x = 1

⇒ 7x − 3 = 0 → 7x = 3 → x = 3/7

**∴ The correct answer is 1 and 3/7.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum and Product of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the **Sum of roots** = −b/a and the **Product of roots** = c/a.

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The value D = b² − 4ac determines the nature: if D > 0, roots are **real and distinct**; if D = 0, roots are **real and equal**; if D < 0, roots are **imaginary**.

Quadratic Formula

Roots can also be calculated using x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)] / 2a.</p

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using a Directory Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure for file systems compared to a simple tree structure?

options.text: DAGs inherently provide better data security and access control.
DAGs reduce disk fragmentation and improve storage efficiency.
DAGs allow for faster traversal and searching of files.
DAGs enable the creation of hard links, allowing a single file to have multiple directory entries.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DAGs enable the creation of hard links, allowing a single file to have multiple directory entries.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) structure allows files to have multiple parent directories, enabling the creation of **hard links**, which are pointers to the same physical file.
 
• Hard links facilitate **efficient file sharing** without duplicating data, reducing storage requirements.
 
• Changes made to a file are reflected across all its hard links, ensuring **consistency** in data access.
 
• Unlike tree structures where files have a single parent directory, DAGs provide **flexibility** in file organization and access paths.
 
• Hard links are widely used in file systems such as **Unix/Linux**, offering a robust mechanism for file management and sharing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG):**

 
 
• A DAG is a graph structure where edges have a direction and there are no cycles (i.e., no path loops back to itself).
 
• It is used in various applications such as file systems, blockchain technology, and task scheduling algorithms.
 
 
 
• **Hard Links vs. Soft Links:**
 
 
• Hard links are pointers to the actual data on the disk and share the same inode number as the original file.
 
• Soft links (symbolic links) are shortcuts that point to the file's location rather than the data itself.
 
• Deleting a file does not affect its hard links, while deleting a target file breaks its symbolic links.
 
 
 
• **File System Hierarchies:**
 
 
• Tree-based file systems enforce a strict parent-child relationship with a single root directory.
 
• DAG-based file systems provide greater flexibility by allowing multiple parent directories for a single file.
 
 
 
• **Unix/Linux File Systems:**
 
 
• Popular file systems like ext4 and NTFS leverage DAG structures to enable advanced features such as hard links and journaling.
 
• DAG structures improve **data accessibility and redundancy** in these operating systems.
 
 
 
• **Applications of DAGs:**
 
 
• DAGs are also extensively used in blockchain technologies like IOTA for transaction validation.
 
• They are critical in representing dependencies in task scheduling systems and computational workflows.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **complementary angles**: 68° + 22° = 90° and 17° + 73° = 90°.

Using **sin²θ + sin²(90°−θ) = 1**, the numerator becomes 1.

Using **cos²θ + cos²(90°−θ) = 1**, the denominator becomes 2(1) = 2.

Result = 1 ÷ 2 = 1/2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (sin² 68^circ + sin² 22^circ)/(2(cos² 17^circ + cos² 73^circ))

**Formula Used:** sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

⇒ Numerator: sin² 68° + sin² (90° − 68°)

questions.question: The shorter side of a rectangle is 24 cm less than the longer side. The numerical value of its area is equal to 8 times the numerical value of its perimeter. What is the length (in cm) of its longer side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **longer side** be L and **shorter side** be (L − 24).

Given: Area = 8 × Perimeter ⇒ L(L − 24) = 8 × 2[L + (L − 24)].

L(L − 24) = 16(2L − 24) ⇒ L² − 24L = 32L − 384.

L² − 56L + 384 = 0 ⇒ (L − 48)(L − 8) = 0.

Since side (L − 24) must be positive, L > 24, so L = 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference between **longer side (L)** and **shorter side (B)** = 24 cm. Area = 8 × Perimeter.

**Formula Used:** Area of rectangle = **L × B**; Perimeter of rectangle = **2(L + B)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48eb247b7b1da0635a9ad76cbae82c260909e9ccf3ac4871e08741c0d5dcf990.png] 

⇒ Let L = x, then B = x − 24.

⇒ Area = x(x − 24).

⇒ Perimeter = 2(x + x − 24) = 2(2x − 24) = 4x − 48.

⇒ According to question: x(x − 24) = 8(4x − 48).

⇒ x² − 24x = 32x − 384.

⇒ x² − 56x + 384 = 0.

⇒ x² − 48x − 8x + 384 = 0.

⇒ x(x − 48) − 8(x − 48) = 0.

⇒ (x − 48)(x − 8) = 0.

⇒ x = 48 or x = 8.

⇒ Since B = x − 24, x cannot be 8 (else B would be negative).

⇒ Longer side L = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rectangle

A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. Opposite sides are equal and parallel. The **diagonal** length is given by √(L² + B²).

Quadratic Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and product of roots is c/a. In x² − 56x + 384 = 0, 48 × 8 = 384 and 48 + 8 = 56.</p

questions.question: Which pair of compounds illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CO and CO₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Law of Multiple Proportions **states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a simple whole-number ratio.
 
• Carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) are compounds of carbon and oxygen that follow this law.
 
• In CO, the ratio of carbon to oxygen by mass is 12:16, while in CO₂, it is 12:32. The oxygen mass ratio between CO and CO₂ is 16:32, which simplifies to 1:2.
 
• This simple whole-number ratio (1:2) illustrates the Law of Multiple Proportions.
 
• The law was proposed by John Dalton in 1804 and is one of the basic principles of stoichiometry in chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:**

 
 
• It is one of the fundamental laws of chemical combination in chemistry.
 
• This law applies when two elements form more than one compound, such as CO and CO₂, or SO₂ and SO₃.
 
• The law emphasizes the discrete nature of chemical combinations, underscoring the concept of fixed proportions in compounds.
 
 
 
• **Examples of the Law:**
 
 
• Water (H₂O) and hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) — The ratio of oxygen masses is 1:2.
 
• Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and sulfur trioxide (SO₃) — The ratio of oxygen masses is 2:3.
 
 
 
• **John Dalton:**
 
 
• He is known as the "Father of Modern Chemistry" for his Atomic Theory, which includes the Law of Multiple Proportions.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern stoichiometry and molecular chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• It is the quantitative study of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
 
• The Law of Multiple Proportions is a cornerstone of stoichiometric calculations.

Area of Parallelogram

questions.question:
What is the median of the following data?

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the given data in **ascending order**: 20, 47, 52, 53, 59, 69, 72, 81, 85, 86, 98.

Count of observations (N) = 11 (which is an **odd number**).

**Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th term = (12 ÷ 2)th term = **6th term**.

The 6th term in the sorted sequence is **69**.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data set: 72, 47, 98, 52, 20, 86, 85, 69, 59, 81, 53

Total number of observations (N) = **11**

**Formula Used:**

When N is odd, **Median** = ((N + 1) ÷ 2)th observation.

When N is even, **Median** = [ (N ÷ 2)th observation + ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th observation ] ÷ 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5819b9a4cd9df52c6b63eac150d4efc7f7e692a8c5ee8a8be7a238be204256de.png] 

**Calculations:**

First, arrange the data in ascending order:

⇒ 20, 47, 52, 53, 59, 69, 72, 81, 85, 86, 98

Since N = 11 (which is an odd number):

⇒ Median = ((11 + 1) ÷ 2)th term

⇒ Median = 6th term

⇒ The 6th term in the sorted list is **69**.

Let us analyze why the other options are incorrect:

⇒ **Option (1) 68.5** is incorrect because it is not the middle value of the sorted dataset.

⇒ **Option (2) 70** is incorrect because 70 is not present in the dataset and is not the median.

⇒ **Option (4) 69.5** is incorrect because it would be the median if the number of terms was even and the two middle terms averaged to 69.5, which is not the case here.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Terms

If the number of observations (N) is even, the median is the average of the (N ÷ 2)th and ((N ÷ 2) + 1)th terms after sorting.

Relation between Mean, Median, and Mode

For a moderately skewed distribution, the empirical relationship is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Properties of Median

The median is not affected by extreme values (outliers) in the dataset, making it a more robust measure of central tendency than the mean for skewed distributions.</p

questions.question: Enzyme cofactors such as NAD+ function mainly by:

options.text: increasing the overall concentration of the enzyme

Cost of 1 **bag** = 206 − 42 = ₹164.

Difference = 6 × 164 − 10 × 42 = 984 − 420 = ₹564.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹564.**

**Given:**

Cost of 3 **bags** and 6 **pens** = ₹744

Now, find the amount by which 6 **bags** exceed 10 **pens**:

⇒ (6 × B) − (10 × P)

⇒ (6 × 164) − (10 × 42)

⇒ 984 − 420

⇒ 564

questions.question: Which of the following components is/are NOT a part of the Central Processing Unit (CPU)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Processing Unit (CPU) consists of three main components: the **Control Unit (CU)**, **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)**, and **Registers**.
 
• The Control Unit (CU) directs the operation of the processor by interpreting instructions and coordinating tasks.
 
• The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs mathematical calculations and logical operations.
 
• Registers are small storage locations within the CPU used to temporarily hold data, instructions, and results.
 
• **Graphic Cards**, on the other hand, are not a part of the CPU. They are separate hardware components designed specifically for rendering images, videos, and 3D graphics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Control Unit (CU):**

 
 
• The CU acts as the "brain" of the CPU, managing the execution of instructions and ensuring all components work in harmony.
 
• It fetches, decodes, and executes instructions stored in memory.
 
 
 
• **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU):**
 
 
• The ALU is responsible for performing arithmetic operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• It also handles logical operations such as comparisons (e.g., greater than, less than, equal to).
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are high-speed storage units within the CPU, used to hold data temporarily during processing.
 
• Examples include the accumulator, instruction register, and program counter.
 
 
 
• **Graphic Card:**
 
 
• A Graphic Card, also known as a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit), is a specialized hardware designed for processing visual data efficiently.
 
• It is used primarily in gaming, video editing, and graphic design tasks, where rendering speed and quality are critical.
 
 
 
• **Difference between CPU and GPU:**
 
 
• While the CPU is designed for general-purpose tasks, the GPU is optimized for parallel processing and high-performance graphical computations.
 
• Modern GPUs also support AI and machine learning workloads due to their parallel architecture.

questions.question: Which Indian freedom fighter was one of the first to openly support Marxist and communist ideologies, and played a pioneering role in the labour movement and the formation of the Communist Party of India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **M N Roy**, originally named Manabendra Nath Bhattacharya, was a prominent Indian revolutionary and political thinker who played a significant role in introducing Marxist and communist ideologies in India.
 
• He co-founded the **Communist Party of India (CPI)** in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, in 1920, making it one of the first communist parties outside the Soviet Union.
 
• Roy actively participated in the international communist movement and was a delegate to the **Comintern (Communist International)**, representing India.
 
• He was a key figure in the Indian labour movement, advocating for workers' rights and the need for organized trade unions to fight against capitalist exploitation.
 
• Roy later became known for his philosophical contributions, particularly his theory of **Radical Humanism**, which sought to reconcile individual freedom with collective social progress.

• Founded in 1925 in Kanpur, the CPI was initially inspired by Marxist-Leninist principles and aimed to overthrow colonial rule through class struggle and revolution.
 
• The party played a significant role in organizing workers, peasants, and trade unions in India during the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Marxism:**
 
 
• An ideology developed by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels that advocates for a classless society through the abolition of private property and the establishment of collective ownership of the means of production.
 
• It emphasizes the role of the working class (proletariat) in overthrowing capitalist systems.
 
 
 
• **Radical Humanism:**
 
 
• A philosophical framework proposed by M N Roy, focusing on individual freedom, rational thinking, and ethical values in building a progressive society.
 
• It rejected authoritarianism, including both capitalism and dogmatic Marxism, while emphasizing human dignity and self-realization.
 
 
 
• **Comintern (Communist International):**
 
 
• Founded in 1919 by Lenin, it was an international organization that advocated for world communism.
 
• It supported revolutionary movements and communist parties globally, including M N Roy’s efforts to establish the CPI.
 
 
 
• **Labour Movement in India:**
 
 
• The labour movement began in the late 19th century and gained momentum during the early 20th century with the rise of trade unions and worker strikes.
 
• Leaders like M N Roy emphasized the importance of uniting workers to demand fair wages, better working conditions, and social justice.

questions.question: A tap fills a cistern in 15 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 17 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill two-third of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net efficiency = 1/15 − 1/17 = (17 − 15) / 255 = 2 / 255 cistern/hour.

Time for full tank = 255 / 2 hours.

Time for 2/3rd tank = (255 / 2) × (2 / 3) = 255 / 3 = 85 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 85 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling Tap (A) = 15 hours, Emptying Tap (B) = 17 hours.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Tap** **Time (hr)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Tap A (+) 15 255 units +17 
 Tap B (−) 17 −15 

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 17 − 15 = 2 units/hour.

⇒ Required filling volume = 2/3 × 255 units = 2 × 85 = 170 units.

⇒ Time required = Required volume ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 170 ÷ 2 = 85 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 85 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency** while emptying pipes (leakages) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Rate Formula

If a pipe fills in 'x' hours and another empties in 'y' hours, net time to fill is (xy) ÷ (y − x) where y > x.

Fractional Work

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of quadrilateral?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A **quadrilateral** is defined as a polygon with exactly **four sides**.

A **trapezoid**, **rhombus**, and **kite** are all 4-sided polygons, which makes them types of quadrilaterals.

An **octagon** is an 8-sided polygon, so it is **NOT** a quadrilateral.

**∴ The correct answer is Octagon.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A list of geometric shapes to classify based on the number of sides.

**Concept:**

Polygons are classified according to the number of sides they possess:

⇒ **Quadrilateral:** 4 sides

⇒ **Octagon:** 8 sides

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8806b7baa97001daad393361d374a070b463d548c1bdba21d46920d8e0e30596.png] 

**Calculations and Analysis:**

⇒ **Trapezoid:** Has 4 sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Rhombus:** Has 4 equal sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Kite:** Has 4 sides with two pairs of equal adjacent sides (Quadrilateral).

⇒ **Octagon:** Has 8 sides.

⇒ Therefore, the octagon does not belong to the quadrilateral family.

**∴ The correct answer is Octagon.**

**__Additional Information__**

Types of Quadrilaterals

Common quadrilaterals include squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses, trapezoids, and kites. The sum of their interior angles is always 360°.

Sum of Interior Angles Formula

The sum of the interior angles of any n-sided polygon is given by (n − 2) × 180°. For an octagon (n = 8), the sum of the interior angles is 1080°.

Polygon Classification

Polygons are named based on their number of sides: Triangle (3), Quadrilateral (4), Pentagon (5), Hexagon (6), Heptagon (7), Octagon (8), Nonagon (9), Decagon (10).</p

Solve the **nested square roots** from the innermost part to the outermost.

√289 = 17

√(125 + 19) = √144 = 12

**Step 2:** Substitute this value back into the expression.

⇒ √(125 + √(344 + 17))

⇒ √(125 + √361)

**Step 3:** Evaluate the next square root.

⇒ √361 = 19 (since 19² = 361)

**Step 4:** Substitute this value and solve the final square root.

⇒ √(125 + 19)

⇒ √144

⇒ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Always simplify the **innermost bracket** or radical sign first before moving to the outer operations.

Unit Digit Trick

questions.question: A 100 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in same direction) in 30 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will this train take to completely cross another 220 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 51 km/hr?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Train − Man) = Distance ÷ Time = 100 m ÷ 30 s = (10/3) m/s.

Convert Man speed to m/s: 9 × 5/18 = 2.5 m/s → **Train Speed** = 10/3 + 2.5 = 35/6 m/s.

Train 2 speed = 51 × 5/18 = 85/6 m/s. Combined Speed (Opposite) = 35/6 + 85/6 = 20 m/s.

**Required Time** = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = (100 + 220) ÷ 20 = 16 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72c778221a41dfa1a09841614c202bb178097f0671a3713f3e5ddf044dde2b34.png] 

**Given:** Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 100 m, Man speed = 9 km/hr, Time = 30 s. Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 220 m, Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = 51 km/hr.

**Formula:** Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time; km/hr to m/s = Multiply by 5/18.

⇒ Speed of man in m/s = 9 × (5/18) = 2.5 m/s.

⇒ Let Train 1 speed be S₁. (S₁ − 2.5) = 100/30.

⇒ S₁ = 10/3 + 2.5 = 35/6 m/s.

⇒ Speed of Train 2 in m/s = 51 × (5/18) = 85/6 m/s.

⇒ Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 35/6 + 85/6 = 120/6 = 20 m/s.

⇒ Time to cross each other = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ Relative Speed = (100 + 220) ÷ 20 = 320 ÷ 20 = 16 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When moving in the **same direction**, subtract speeds (S₁ − S₂). In **opposite directions**, add speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Distance

Total distance while crossing a **pole/man** is the train length. Total distance while crossing **another train/platform** is the sum of both lengths.</p

questions.question: Find the average of all prime numbers between 20 and 40.
questions.solution:

Total count of numbers = 4.

Average = 120 ÷ 4 = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

⇒ Prime numbers between 20 and 40 are: **23, 29, 31, 37**.

⇒ Sum = 23 + 29 + 31 + 37

⇒ Sum = 120

⇒ Number of terms (n) = 4

⇒ Average = 120 ÷ 4

⇒ Average = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

questions.question: If 4 : 16 :: 7.3 : x and 4 : 32 :: 7 : y. What is the ratio of x to y?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For the first proportion 4 : 16 :: 7.3 : x, the multiplier is 4 (since 4 × 4 = 16), so **x** = 7.3 × 4 = 29.2.

For the second proportion 4 : 32 :: 7 : y, the multiplier is 8 (since 4 × 8 = 32), so **y** = 7 × 8 = 56.

Ratio **x : y** = 29.2 : 56 = 292 : 560 = 73 : 140.

**∴ The correct answer is 73 : 140.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d321fb8d472a097f302531568938b9e33287249b34ae2f57946eee4d1ddc7ca0.png] 

**Given:** First proportion 4 : 16 :: 7.3 : x and Second proportion 4 : 32 :: 7 : y.

**Formula Used:** If a : b :: c : d, then **Product of Extremes = Product of Means** (a × d = b × c).

⇒ For 4 : 16 :: 7.3 : x: 4 × x = 16 × 7.3

⇒ x = (16 × 7.3) ÷ 4 = 4 × 7.3 = 29.2

⇒ For 4 : 32 :: 7 : y: 4 × y = 32 × 7

⇒ y = (32 × 7) ÷ 4 = 8 × 7 = 56

⇒ Ratio x : y = 29.2 : 56

⇒ Multiplying by 10 to remove decimal: 292 : 560

⇒ Dividing by 4: 73 : 140

**∴ The correct answer is 73 : 140.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: c : d, the term **d** is called the fourth proportional, calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

In a continued proportion a : b :: b : c, the term **c** is the third proportional, where c = b² ÷ a.</p

questions.question: A water tank can be filled in 38 minutes by using 44 pipes of the same capacity. In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 37 pipes of the same capacity as above?

Total work = **Pipes × Time**

⇒ 1672 = 37 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 1672 ÷ 37

⇒ D₂ = 45.1891...

⇒ D₂ ≈ 45.19 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 45.19 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion

When the number of pipes increases, the time taken to fill the tank decreases, following the relation M₁T₁ = M₂T₂.

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Total capacity is treated as constant work. Efficiency is directly proportional to the number of identical pipes used.</p

• This constitutional mechanism ensures a balance between the executive's decision-making power and the President's oversight role.
 
• The provision highlights the President's role as a constitutional head, who must act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

• It defines the Prime Minister's duties concerning communication between the President and the Council of Ministers.
 
• It mandates the Prime Minister to keep the President informed of all decisions of the Cabinet related to the administration of India.
 
• The article ensures the President is aware of the governance and policy decisions while maintaining a ceremonial role.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Indian Parliamentary Democracy**
 
 
• The President is the constitutional head of state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President's role is largely ceremonial, with real executive power resting with the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Reconsideration Mechanism**
 
 
• The mechanism allows the President to return legislative and executive proposals for reconsideration.
 
• It is a tool to ensure thorough deliberation by the Cabinet, especially in cases of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Checks and Balances**
 
 
• India's parliamentary democracy incorporates checks and balances to prevent the misuse of power.

questions.question: Which of the given tribal uprisings did NOT take place around the unrest during the Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birsa Munda Revolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Birsa Munda Revolt**, also known as the Ulgulan (The Great Tumult), occurred in the late 19th century (1899–1900) and was not connected to the Revolt of 1857.
 
• This revolt was led by **Birsa Munda**, a tribal leader from the Munda community, in the Chotanagpur region (present-day Jharkhand).
 
• The rebellion primarily aimed at resisting British colonial exploitation and missionary interference in tribal lands and culture.
 
• Birsa Munda's movement focused on the restoration of tribal rights over their land (Khuntkatti system) and rejecting oppressive British laws.
 
• Unlike the other uprisings mentioned, which were closely linked to the broader unrest during the Revolt of 1857, the Birsa Munda Revolt was a localized tribal movement in the late 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This revolt was led by Veer Surendra Sai against British rule in Sambalpur (present-day Odisha).
 
• It was closely linked to the larger Revolt of 1857 and aimed at overthrowing British authority in the region.
 
• Surendra Sai fought for the restoration of local tribal and princely rights.
 
 
 
• **Naikda Movement (1857–1858):**
 
 
• This tribal uprising occurred in Gujarat during the Revolt of 1857.
 
• The Naikda tribe resisted British policies that disrupted their traditional lifestyle and autonomy.
 
• It was a localized movement but inspired by the general anti-colonial sentiment of 1857.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Rebellion (1855–1856):**
 
 
• Led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, the Santhal Rebellion took place in the Rajmahal Hills (present-day Jharkhand).
 
• It was a precursor to the Revolt of 1857 and aimed at resisting oppressive zamindari systems and British policies.
 
• The Santhal tribes fought for their rights to land and freedom from exploitative moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Movements in India:**
 
 
• Tribal uprisings were often reactions to exploitation by British policies, zamindars, and moneylenders.
 
• Most tribal revolts were rooted in issues like land alienation, forced labor, and cultural interference.
 
• These movements highlight the resilience and struggles of indigenous communities against colonial oppression.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean proportional between **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

First term (a) = (18 + 10√7)

Second term (b) = (18 − 4√7)

Mean Proportional = √(a × b)

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[(18 + 10√7) × (18 − 4√7)]

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[18(18 − 4√7) + 10√7(18 − 4√7)]

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[324 − 72√7 + 180√7 − (10 × 4 × 7)]

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[324 + 108√7 − 280]

⇒ Mean Proportional = √[44 + 108√7]

**∴ The correct answer is √(44 + 108√7).**

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion, then c is the third proportional and c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a:b = c:d), then d is the fourth proportional and d = (b × c)/a.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a:b is a²:b² and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a:√b.</p

questions.question: In modern motherboards, which component is directly connected to the CPU to facilitate high-speed communication?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northbridge**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northbridge is a chipset on the motherboard that acts as the primary interface between the CPU and high-speed components like RAM and GPUs.
 
• It facilitates high-speed communication between the CPU and the system's memory (RAM), as well as graphics controllers.
 
• In modern systems, the Northbridge is often integrated directly into the CPU itself, enhancing efficiency and reducing latency.
 
• It plays a critical role in ensuring smooth data transfer between the CPU and other high-performance components.
 
• Over time, the Northbridge has become less distinct as newer technologies like System-on-Chip (SoC) designs integrate its functions directly into the processor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chipset Architecture**

 
 
• A motherboard's chipset typically consists of two main components: the Northbridge and the Southbridge.
 
• The Northbridge handles high-speed communication with the CPU, RAM, and GPU, while the Southbridge manages peripheral devices like I/O ports and storage.
 
 
 
• **Modern Replacements**
 
 
• In modern motherboards, the Northbridge's functions are integrated into the CPU die, eliminating the need for a separate chipset.
 
• This integration is commonly seen in Intel's Core series processors and AMD's Ryzen processors.
 
 
 
• **System-on-Chip (SoC) Design**
 
 
• In SoC designs, the CPU, Northbridge, and GPU are integrated into a single chip for better performance and power efficiency.
 
• This design is prevalent in mobile devices, laptops, and compact systems.
 
 
 
• **PCIe Connectivity**
 
 
• Modern Northbridge functionality includes managing PCI Express (PCIe) lanes, which connect GPUs and other high-speed expansion cards.
 
• PCIe provides a high-bandwidth interface, crucial for modern gaming and data-intensive applications.
 
 
 
• **Memory Controller Integration**
 
 
• In older systems, the Northbridge housed the memory controller, but modern CPUs integrate the memory controller directly into the processor.
 
• This change improves memory access speed and reduces latency significantly.

questions.question: Green Revolution technologies heavily relied on inputs and were scale-sensitive. Why did small and marginal farmers face challenges in adopting Green Revolution technologies?

options.text: High input costs and credit inaccessibility

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High input costs and credit inaccessibility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Green Revolution technologies required substantial investments in high-yield seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation systems, which were expensive for small and marginal farmers.
 
• Access to institutional credit was limited for small farmers due to lack of collateral, making it difficult for them to secure loans for purchasing inputs.
 
• High input costs were not feasible for marginal farmers who generally operated on subsistence-level incomes and lacked savings to invest in advanced agricultural technologies.
 
• Small landholdings posed challenges in achieving economies of scale, further exacerbating the financial burden of adopting Green Revolution technologies.
 
• As a result, the benefits of the Green Revolution were concentrated among medium and large-scale farmers, widening the economic disparity in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a series of agricultural innovations introduced during the 1960s and 1970s, aimed at increasing food production to combat hunger.
 
• It involved the use of high-yield variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• India benefited significantly, especially in wheat and rice production, turning the country from a food importer to a self-sufficient nation in food grains.
 
 
 
• **Challenges for Marginal Farmers:**
 
 
• Marginal farmers are defined as those owning less than 1 hectare (2.5 acres) of land.
 
• They often lack access to credit facilities, modern equipment, and technical knowledge required for high-yield farming.
 
• Their dependence on rain-fed agriculture further increases their vulnerability to climate variations.
 
 
 
• **Institutional Credit:**
 
 
• Institutional credit refers to loans provided by banks, cooperatives, and government-backed financial institutions.
 
• In India, schemes like Kisan Credit Card (KCC) aim to provide easy access to credit for farmers.
 
• Despite such initiatives, small farmers often face barriers such as lack of collateral or insufficient documentation.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Green Revolution:**
 
 
• While the Green Revolution increased food production, it also led to environmental issues like soil degradation and water scarcity.
 
• It created regional disparities, with states like Punjab and Haryana benefiting more compared to others.
 
• The reliance on chemical inputs led to long-term health and ecological concerns.

questions.question: The total length of the Northern Plain of India from west to east is approximately ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2400 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plain of India spans approximately **2400 km** in length from west to east, extending through the states of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by three major river systems: **the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra**.
 
• It is one of the world's most fertile regions and forms a significant part of the **Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain**.
 
• The plain is broadly divided into three sections: the Punjab Plains in the west, the Ganga Plains in the center, and the Brahmaputra Plains in the east.
 
• This region is characterized by alluvial soil, making it ideal for agriculture, and it supports a dense population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is the predominant soil type in the Northern Plain, deposited by rivers over thousands of years.
 
• It is rich in nutrients such as potash, phosphoric acid, and lime, making it highly fertile.
 
• The soil supports the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers, along with their tributaries, play a crucial role in shaping the plain.
 
• These rivers provide water for irrigation and contribute to the alluvial deposits.
 
 
 
• **Physiographic Divisions of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Northern Plain is divided into the Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, and Khadar regions based on their geological characteristics.
 
• Khadar (new alluvium) is the most fertile and is renewed annually by river floods.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plain is often referred to as the "Granary of India" due to its high agricultural output.
 
• It is also home to major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow, making it a hub for trade and commerce.

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹8,000, **Amount (A)** = ₹15,625, **Time (t)** = 1 year 6 months = 1.5 years.

For **half-yearly compounding**, n = 1.5 × 2 = 3 periods.

⇒ 15625 = 8000(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 1 + r/100 = 5/4

⇒ r/100 = 5/4 − 1 = 1/4

⇒ r = 25% (half-yearly rate)

⇒ **Annual Rate (R)** = 2 × r = 2 × 25% = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

Compounding Frequency

It is the actual annual interest rate when compounding occurs more than once a year: **Rₑff = [(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1] × 100**.

questions.question: In March 2025, India's Parliament passed the Bills of Lading Bill, 2025. What was the primary objective of this legislation?

options.text: To modernise the 169 years old shipping law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To modernise the 169 years old shipping law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Parliament passed the **Bills of Lading Bill, 2025** to modernise the **169-year-old shipping laws** and align them with current international shipping practices.
 
• The bill replaces the **Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856**, which was outdated and did not reflect advancements in the shipping industry.
 
• The legislation introduces **digital bills of lading**, allowing electronic documentation and reducing the dependency on physical paperwork in maritime trade.
 
• It aims to boost **efficiency and transparency** in maritime logistics, facilitating faster and more secure trade documentation processes.
 
• The new framework ensures India's shipping laws comply with **global maritime conventions**, fostering better trade relationships with international partners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bills of Lading:**

 
 
• A bill of lading is a legal document issued by a carrier to a shipper, detailing the type, quantity, and destination of goods being transported.
 
• It serves as proof of shipment, a receipt of goods, and a document of title, enabling ownership transfer during trade.
 
 
 
• **Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856:**
 
 
• This act governed bills of lading in India for over 169 years, but was increasingly inadequate for modern maritime trade needs.
 
• The act lacked provisions for electronic documentation and modern dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Digital Bills of Lading:**
 
 
• Digital bills of lading enable electronic issuance, transfer, and verification of documents, reducing fraud and operational delays.
 
• This shift aligns with global trends in **e-commerce and digitisation of trade**.
 
 
 
• **Global Maritime Trade:**
 
 
• The shipping industry handles approximately **80% of global trade** by volume, making efficient legislation critical for economic growth.
 
• Modern laws ensure compliance with conventions like the **United Nations Convention on the Carriage of Goods by Sea** (Hamburg Rules).

questions.question: The evidence of the earliest cotton cultivation in the Indus valley is found at which site?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mehrgarh**, located in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan, is one of the earliest sites of human settlement and farming in South Asia.
 
• Evidence of the **earliest cultivation of cotton** has been found at Mehrgarh, dating back to approximately 6000 BCE.
 
• Archaeological excavations at Mehrgarh have uncovered remains of cotton seeds, fabrics, and tools used for spinning and weaving.
 
• The site provides critical insights into the development of agriculture and textile production in the pre-Indus Valley Civilization era.
 
• Mehrgarh is considered a precursor to the mature Harappan Civilization, showcasing early advancements in agriculture, animal domestication, and crafts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC):**

 
 
• The IVC, also known as the Harappan Civilization, flourished around 2600–1900 BCE in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It is known for its advanced urban planning, including well-laid streets, drainage systems, and architectural innovations.
 
 
 
• **Mehrgarh's Significance:**
 
 
• Mehrgarh is one of the oldest sites with evidence of farming, herding, and craft specialization in South Asia.
 
• The settlement also shows early evidence of dentistry, with drilled teeth found in human remains.
 
 
 
• **Cotton Cultivation in Ancient Times:**
 
 
• Cotton, known as "tree wool," was one of the first fibers cultivated by humans for textile production.
 
• The use of cotton eventually spread from South Asia to the Middle East, Egypt, and later to Europe.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Sites:**
 
 
• **Harappa:** Known for urban planning and advanced drainage systems.
 
• **Kalibangan:** Famous for its fire altars and ploughed field remains.
 
• **Rakhigarhi:** One of the largest known Harappan sites in India.

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchased 59 dozens of articles at the rate of ₹728 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹91. What percentage profit did he make?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Cost Price (CP)** of 1 article = 728 ÷ 12 = ₹182/3.

**Selling Price (SP)** of 1 article = ₹91.

Ratio of **CP : SP** = (182/3) : 91 = 182 : 273 = 2 : 3.

Profit = 3 − 2 = 1 unit on 2 units of CP.

**Profit%** = (1 ÷ 2) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP of 1 dozen = ₹728 | SP of 1 article = ₹91 | 1 dozen = 12 articles.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95964cc96cff4eab1bc9358bb6c9f794b8529ddef9dea62dd147da1b1c46ce5f.png] 

⇒ **CP per article** = Total CP ÷ Number of articles = 728 ÷ 12 = ₹60.666...

⇒ **SP per article** = ₹91.

⇒ **Profit per article** = 91 − (728/12) = (1092 − 728) ÷ 12 = 364 ÷ 12 = ₹91/3.

⇒ **Profit%** = [(91/3) ÷ (728/12)] × 100 = [91/3 × 12/728] × 100.

⇒ **Profit%** = [1/1 × 4/8] × 100 = 1/2 × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Independence in Profit%

Profit percentage is a **relative measure**. It remains the same whether calculated for a single item, a dozen, or the entire stock, provided the rate remains constant.

Profit and Loss Formula

When **SP > CP**, it is Profit. When **CP > SP**, it is Loss. **Loss%** = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.
